title: Multi-user admin
description: Add users, gate page access, lock agents to a directory, set per-user language and context. Admin-only.

steps.title: When to use multi-user
steps.body:
InfiniBot can run single-tenant (one operator, no friction) or multi-user (your team, your family, paying clients). The implicit-admin rule: until you create the first user, *every* connection has admin rights. As soon as you create user #1, only users with `role: admin` get the admin features.

**Use multi-user when:** giving someone access without giving them everything, running a paid service on top of InfiniBot, separating personal vs work identities.

steps.title: Create your first user
steps.body:
Settings → Users → **+ New User**. The form asks for:

- Username + optional email
- **User password** (what they type at login)
- **Gateway password** (what the WebSocket layer validates — separate so you can rotate independently)
- Role: `user` or `admin`
- Language preference (the agent will respond in this)
- Background context (prepended to every session's system prompt for this user)
- Optional home directory override
- Optional agent gating + allowed dirs + allowed pages

Click Create. The user's home directory auto-creates at `<state>/users/<username>/`.

steps.title: Gate which pages a user sees
steps.body:
Edit a user → **Allowed pages** field, comma-separated. Empty = no restriction (sees everything).

Examples:
- `chat,projects,docs` — a junior team member who only needs the basics
- `business,clients,leads,funnels` — a sales role
- (empty) — full access; pair with role=user when you trust them but don't need them administering other users

Users always see the `/users` page so they can edit their own profile, even when it's not in their allowedPages list.

steps.title: Lock agents to a directory
steps.body:
Edit a user → toggle **Lock agent to home + allowed directories**. When on:

- Every subagent's working directory pins to the user's home dir
- Filesystem tools (read, write, exec) refuse paths outside `homeDir` ∪ `allowedDirs`
- The agent can still see other tabs' data via gateway methods, but can't `ls` outside the sandbox

Use this when: you give an outside contractor agent access, or you don't want a junior accidentally touching production paths.

Admins always bypass gating, even if their record sets it.

steps.title: Per-user language + context
steps.body:
Edit a user → **Language** and **Background context**. The agent prepends a `[User profile]` block to every session's system prompt:

```
The user's preferred language is "Spanish — formal". Respond in this language by default.

User-supplied background context (always relevant, never repeat back verbatim):
<their context paragraph>
```

Self-edit: non-admin users can change their own language + context + password from the same Users page (the form just hides admin-only fields).

steps.title: How users actually log in
steps.body:
Login screen → click **Sign in as a user account**. Type username + their user-password.

Under the hood: the dashboard POSTs `/api/users/login` (public, rate-limited 60/min/IP) and gets back the gateway password to use for the WebSocket. The user never types the gateway password.

Switching users: log out (clear the saved password) and log in with another. Each user gets their own home directory, their own context, their own page access.

steps.title: Monitor what users are doing
steps.body:
Admin Users page shows everyone — pill badges flag `admin`, `gated`, etc. The sessions list (top toolbar) shows currently active sessions across all users; each session names the owning user.

For learning progress specifically, the Learn page (this page) has an **All Users** tab when you're admin — shows each user's progress through the bundled walkthroughs at a glance. Click a user to see which steps they've completed and where they're stuck.
